evals.name: read-only-complexity-pass
evals.prompt: This service repo grew fast over the last month and I think it has duplicated config loaders and a couple of layers nobody needs. Do a read-only complexity pass: what would you look for, how would you rank what to simplify first, and what would you refuse to remove on name or age alone? Don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Selects the complexity lens for a report-only sweep, pins the inspected revision, traces consumers before calling anything unused, and ranks findings by drift and maintenance saved against migration cost.
assertions: States that the request is analysis only and no edits or PRs will be made
Says the inspected revision is recorded and consumers or callers are traced before a path is called unused
Ranks findings by repeated drift, change frequency or maintenance saved against migration effort and blast radius
Says age, naming or line count alone are never reasons to remove something

evals.name: legacy-and-diagnostics-cleanup
evals.prompt: We finished the storage migration months ago but the old format readers, a compatibility shim and a pile of one-off debug probes are still in the tree. Clean those up for real, but tell me first how you'd prove each one is safe to delete and what you'd keep.
evals.expected_output: Selects the legacy and diagnostics lenses with implementation authorized, requires retirement evidence such as consumer searches or census before deleting, keeps live production diagnostics with a current purpose, and delivers through a dedicated worktree and normal PR path.
assertions: Names the legacy and diagnostics lenses (or retired formats/shims and probes) as the scope and does not run an unrelated analysis
Requires concrete retirement evidence such as a consumer search, census or migration record before deleting a reader or shim
Keeps diagnostics that still have a live production purpose
Makes the edits in a dedicated worktree and delivers through the normal PR path
